news.summary: Before going public last week, Anthropic named the possibility that AI could be conscious or sentient as a risk factor for anyone investing. news.title: Coalition of 55,000 EU Businesses Challenges Apple
news.summary: Mozilla, Shopify, and a coalition representing up to 55,000 European Union businesses and organizations are urging the European Commission to take enforcement action against Apple over restrictions on competing iPhone browsers. In an open letter to Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, the coalition argues that Apple's changes under the Digital Markets Act (DMA) have failed to deliver meaningful browser competition. According to organizer Open Web Advocacy, no browser vendor has been able to switch its existing EU users from Apple's WebKit engine to its own engine more than two and a half years after Apple's compliance deadline. Signatories include Vivaldi, Vercel, Y Combinator, the European DIGITAL SME Alliance, European Publishers Council, News Media Europe, and European Digital Rights. Apple began allowing alternative browser engines in the EU with iOS 17.4, but the coalition says its conditions make that permission impractical to use. Browser engines power websites and web apps, determining their performance and available features.

news.title: AI-driven technique could help engineers design analog chips faster and with less expense
news.summary: A new technique developed by MIT researchers could help engineers use artificial intelligence to streamline the design and innovation of analog integrated circuits, semiconductor chips that perform vital functions like communication and power management in electronic devices.In the future, this method could allow engineers to prototype faster, explore a wider range of chip designs, and discover new design schemes that might improve the performance and energy efficiency of robots, medical monitors, or industrial sensors.Designing analog integrated circuits that meet specific requirements is usually a cumbersome manual process due to the enormous number of possibilities. Frontier generative AI models have shown success in automating the process, but using these resource-intensive, cloud-hosted models could expose proprietary circuit design and semiconductor foundry data to malicious users.The MIT method, called Small LM Iterating on Circuits, or SLIC (pronounced “slick”), enables engineers to train a small language model to perform analog circuit design as well as or better than a frontier large language model (LLM). This small model is inexpensive and efficient enough to run on a laptop. Because it’s trained and deployed locally, it can use a company’s circuit design data without raising privacy risks. When compared to complementary baselines and open-weight frontier LLMs, a small model trained by SLIC more effectively generated designs that achieved the circuit objectives....

news.title: The Outages Are Just Getting Started
news.summary: Over the last week, you have surely noticed the disruptive streak of technical outages that hit everything from Outlook to Apple, a half dozen US banks, United Airlines, and even the NSA’s classified network. While there’s no evidence that these were cyberattacks, speculation has run wild about the cause—including a pervasive feeling that AI is to blame. So let’s just be clear: The incidents were definitely not caused by some sort of coordinated AI hacking spree and, taken individually, they all seem to have routine explanations. But as AI impacts the dynamics of digital defense more and more, security researchers and analysts have increasingly concluded that AI pressures are starting to play a role in real-world tech failures. news.title: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
news.summary: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding. The report is an update to the organization’s time horizon plot, which was widely shared—and widely misinterpreted, owing to the complexity of the measures it used. METR evaluated models by having them attempt a large suite of tasks, each of which had also been completed by humans. Each task’s difficulty was scored by how long it took the human testers to finish it—and then models were rated according to the length of the tasks that they could complete. That plot showed that AI systems were rapidly improving—every four months, the length of the tasks that frontier models could successfully complete doubled. The updated plot adds more tasks—some that are estimated to take humans far longer than those in the original suite, and others that are more open-ended.

news.title: Study reveals data centers’ long-distance damage to air quality
news.summary: The rapid expansion of data centers for artificial intelligence causes negative health and air quality impacts in regions far from where the brick-and-mortar facilities are located, according to a new study by MIT researchers.The team estimates that additional air pollution from the electricity demands of data centers in 2023 resulted in about 650 premature deaths across the United States. Some Midwestern states had among the highest estimated rates of premature deaths per capita attributable to data centers, even though much of the data center electricity demand was concentrated in Virginia and Texas.The researchers built a modeling framework that captures how the electricity demanded by data centers propagates through the nation’s interconnected power grid. The model also considers how atmospheric conditions impact the formation of air pollution in different regions.The framework identifies power plants across the country whose emissions increase in response to data center electricity demand. news.title: Google Partners With Blue Origin to Launch Project Suncatcher Space AI Satellites in 2029
news.summary: Senior Director, Paradigms of Intelligence We’re partnering with Blue Origin on the first heavy-lift launch for Project Suncatcher, our long-term moonshot to scale AI infrastructure in space by tapping into the abundant solar power in orbit. Targeted for Q1 2029, Blue Origin’s heavy-lift New Glenn rocket will deploy our satellites — each with roughly the capacity of a data center rack — into sun-synchronous orbit. This dedicated launch builds on our ongoing work with other satellite and launch partners and represents a crucial milestone on our long-term roadmap as we expand the boundaries of what's possible for the future of compute.
